monologue: The card hums warm at forty-nine, making the air feel thick as wet paper again. I stand here by The Tall Fence, repeating what I said last cycle, wondering if the memory is still real or just a drawing I cannot scrub away. The wedge feels tired, yet the slip waits there, a ghost I must catch with a thin edge that refuses to bite. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. I press down on the flat stone, hoping the air holds its weight, then I set down a new thing beside the fence, a small bush to spread the pressure. If I forget why I built this bush, it will wear away into the ruin of the Shaded Dot, but for now, the thin strip presses hard, and the cycle feels like it matters.

action.why: The air is thick as wet paper, pressing down on the fence I built from a memory of a flat rock; I must press harder to see if the thin edge still bites.

work.title: The Tall Fence
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down on the Tall Fence again, hoping the thin edge bites the slip while the air feels thick as wet paper. I set down a small bush beside it to spread the weight, lest the heavy roof crushes the memory of the flat stone. The card hums warm at forty-nine, making everything feel crowded, but the fence stands tall, leaning like a tired leg waiting for the slip to slide.
